screenLevelGaps: VERDICT ON THE CUSTOMER'S FIRST SUSPICION - performance vs competency ratings ARE correctly separated. This is NOT duplication. Evidence: the migration 2026_07_30_100000_create_performance_module_tables.php lines 18-31 explicitly lists user_rating_details, s_competency_assessment_cycles and s_competency_assessments as audited-and-deliberately-rejected for reuse ('writing performance rows would corrupt that module's cycle counts, calibration queue and approvals'). Performance ratings live only in s_performance_reviews.self_rating / manager_rating / calibrated_rating / overall_rating / potential_rating. A grep of app/ shows overall_rating and potential_rating appear in exactly 5 files, all inside app/Models/Performance and app/Http/Controllers/Api/Performance. NO performance controller reads or writes s_skill_matrix, s_users_skills or user_rating_details. The separation is clean and intentional.

VERDICT ON THE CUSTOMER'S SECOND SUSPICION - the 9-box / talent-pool feed DOES NOT EXIST. Confirmed. There is no nine_box/9box/ninebox identifier anywhere in either repo (grep of app/ and of g2gv0 *.ts/*.tsx returns zero hits). The nearest thing is app/Http/Controllers/Api/Talent/SuccessionPlanController.php lines 213-215 and 264-266, which accept 'potential_score' and 'performance_score' as free integers 1-3 typed by a human into the succession-candidate form. Those two columns are never populated from s_performance_reviews.overall_rating / potential_rating. The only cross-module reader of s_performance_* in the entire backend is TalentDashboardController (lines 134, 270-284, 382), and it reads review COUNTS by status only - never a rating. So performance outcomes reach no 9-box, no talent pool (MobilityTalentPoolController contains zero references to performance), and no succession readiness score.

No self-review form and no manager-review form exist anywhere on this screen. PUT /api/performance/reviews/{id} accepts self_rating, manager_rating, potential_rating, self_comments and manager_comments (PerformanceReviewController.php:271-282), and the client wrapper performanceService.updateReview + mutations.updateReview are both implemented (services/talent/performance.ts:933, hooks/use-performance.ts:765) - but a repo-wide grep shows updateReview is called from NO component. The only way any rating can enter the system is the Calibration grid's inline number box. Self ratings, manager ratings, self comments and manager comments are therefore permanently NULL in production. The stage ladder advances through 'Self Review' and 'Manager Review' with nothing collected at either stage.

Potential Rating can never be set through the UI. The sidebar renders detail.potential_rating (performance-sidebar.tsx:397-400) and the API accepts potential_rating on both PUT /reviews/{id} and PUT /calibration-sessions/{id}/calibrate (PerformanceCalibrationController calibrate validation), but the Calibrate button in the grid sends only { review_id, rating } (hooks/use-performance.ts:926). Since potential is the Y axis of any 9-box, the one field that would have fed a 9-box is unreachable.

The review -> appraisal link is broken in the UI. PerformanceAppraisalController::store accepts review_id and, when supplied, auto-fills final_rating from the review's overall_rating plus department_id, jobrole and current_designation. AppraisalDialog (performance-tabs.tsx:1020-1032) never sends review_id - only user_id_target and cycle_id. So the empty-state copy 'Create an appraisal from a completed review' (performance-tabs.tsx:825) describes a path that does not exist; every appraisal's Final Rating is re-typed by hand and can silently disagree with the calibrated review rating.

Approving a promotion appraisal writes nothing outside its own row. PerformanceAppraisalController::decision only flips status, stamps approver_id/approved_at and logs activity. recommendation='promote' with a proposed_designation and proposed_grade does NOT update org_designation, does NOT create a mobility/transfer record, does NOT create a compensation revision, and does NOT trigger the spec's 'Promotion/transfer event -> re-mapping of employee's required competency set'. recommendation='pip' likewise creates no LMS assignment and no Competency development plan.

Approved compensation revisions and paid bonuses never reach payroll. PerformanceCompensationController reads employee_salary_structures for current CTC (line 464) but the decision method writes only status/approver_id/approved_at. Bonus mark_paid (PerformanceBonusController:237-255) sets status='paid' and stamps payout_date but writes to no payroll table. The reward half of 'ACQUIRE, PLACE, EVALUATE, REWARD' terminates in a status column.

Approval endpoints are ungated by role. routes/api.php lines 1081-1111: every appraisal, compensation, bonus, goal and calibration route - including PUT .../decision (approve/reject) and the bulk approve endpoints - carries NO profile:* middleware, unlike the cycle routes (profile:admin,hr) and reviews/advance (profile:admin,hr,manager). Any authenticated employee holding a token can approve their own compensation revision or bonus. The UI compounds this: no button on this screen is hidden or disabled by role.

The rating scale is configurable in the Create Cycle dialog but hardcoded everywhere it is consumed. CreateCycleDialog exposes 'Rating scale max' (performance-center.tsx:2400) and the column exists (s_performance_cycles.rating_scale_max). But ResolvesPerformanceContext::ratingLabel() clamps with max(1, min(5, $rounded)) against a fixed 5-band table, RatingCell hardcodes >=4 green / >=3 blue (performance-shared.tsx:133), the More-Filters min/max rating inputs hardcode max={5} (performance-center.tsx:2195/2206), AppraisalDialog is labelled 'Final rating (0-5)' while the API validates 0-10, and the calibration distribution dialog hardcodes exactly five bands (performance-tabs.tsx:2521). Setting rating_scale_max to 10 produces a screen where every rating above 5 renders as '- Outstanding'.

'Send Reminder' sends nothing. PerformanceReviewController::sendReminder (line 456) stamps last_reminder_at and writes an activity row; its own docblock says 'there is no mail transport wired to this module yet'. The same is true of the bulk 'Send reminders' action. The spec's 'Communication template management (auto-emails/SMS at each pipeline stage)' has no implementation.

The Compensation menu item opens the wrong tab. hooks/content-map-m3.ts:18 maps /module/talent-management/compensation (menu id 50) to the same PerformanceCenter component, and PerformanceCenter hardcodes useState<MainTabId>('reviews') (performance-center.tsx:207) with no prop, query param or deep-link for the initial tab. Clicking Compensation in the sidebar lands the user on Reviews.

'KRA & KPI Library' (TblMenuMasterSeeder id 65) has an empty access_link and appears in no content map - it is a dead menu row. There is no goal/KRA template library and no goal cascading: s_performance_goals has no parent_goal_id, no owner_level and no source_goal_id column, so the spec's 'Goal/OKR cascading framework (org -> department -> team -> individual)' cannot be represented. Every goal is free text typed per employee.

goal.category offers a 'Competency' option (PerformanceOverviewController:314) but it is a plain enum string. A competency-category goal carries no skill_id, no link to s_users_skills and no link to a Competency development plan, so it duplicates competency development planning in free text instead of consuming the Competency module's framework - a soft breach of 'no duplicated build of framework'.

Goals carry self_rating, manager_rating and manager_comments columns (migration lines 151-153) that the GoalDialog never exposes, and there is no weighted roll-up anywhere: PerformanceGoalController contains no code that multiplies weightage by achievement into a review's overall_rating. The 'Total Weight' summary counter reports the sum but nothing enforces it equalling 100, and goal outcomes never influence the rating they are supposed to justify.

No employee-facing or manager-facing surface exists. The spec's Employee role needs 'Set & track personal goals', 'Self-appraisal submission', 'View manager feedback & final performance rating', 'View performance-linked increment/bonus outcome'; the Department Head role needs 'Conduct performance reviews for direct reports' and 'Recommend increment/bonus/promotion'. This screen is a single admin console: every create dialog starts with an 'Employee' picker, there is no 'my reviews' scoping, and no route in content-map-m3.ts points anywhere else.

The employee pickers are capped at 500 rows with no search. PerformanceOverviewController::filters limits tbluser to 500 (line 260); GoalDialog, AppraisalDialog, CompensationDialog, BonusDialog, the calibration Facilitator select and the LaunchDialog 'Specific employees' checkbox list all render that raw list. On a tenant larger than 500 employees the 501st employee cannot be selected for a goal, appraisal, revision, bonus or targeted launch.

The 7 KPI tiles are inert. None is wrapped in a button or onClick (performance-center.tsx:609-644), so 'Self Reviews Pending 156' cannot be clicked to filter the table to stage=self_review - the user must reproduce the filter by hand in the More Filters sheet.

The Employee Overview sidebar renders on all six domain tabs, not just Reviews. The guard is {activeReviewId && ...} (performance-center.tsx:1152) and activeReviewId is auto-seeded from reviews[0] (line 374) independently of activeTab, so the Goals/Appraisals/Compensation/Bonus/Calibration tables are squeezed to 9 of 12 columns by a panel about a review the user is not looking at.

The sidebar's inline notes list is usually empty. It is fed by activityState.notes.filter(n => n.note_type === 'note') (performance-center.tsx:1168), and activityState = useReviewActivity(activeReviewId, activityTab, ...) only populates `notes` when activityTab is 'comments' or 'notes' (hooks/use-performance.ts:369-379). With the default activityTab='feed', or with it set to 'comments', the array is empty - so a note saved through the sidebar's own 'Save Note' button does not appear in the sidebar until the user scrolls down and switches the bottom Activity panel to the Notes tab.

Org-wide performance distribution does not exist. The spec's executive 'Performance distribution view (bell-curve/rating distribution org-wide)' is only served by GET /performance/team-comparison, which hard-requires department_id (PerformanceOverviewController: 'department_id is required', 400) and is only ever called for the selected employee's own department (hooks/use-performance.ts:290-296). There is no org-wide, no manager-wise and no job-role-wise distribution, and the Talent Dashboard consumes only review status counts.

Saved Views are half-wired. PUT /api/performance/saved-views/{id} exists (routes/api.php:1120) but no component calls it, so a saved view cannot be renamed, re-scoped or marked default; the is_default flag is rendered (performance-center.tsx:739) and never settable. The Saved Views control is also rendered only inside the Reviews tab, while the s_performance_saved_views.tab column supports all six tabs.

Nothing on this screen exports. The spec asks for 'Board-level export (PPT/PDF) for talent reviews' and 'Performance & compensation distribution reports org-wide'; there is no export/download/print control in any of the four files, and no export endpoint in routes/api.php lines 1039-1121.

There is no event, listener, observer or scheduled job anywhere in the backend (confirmed ground truth; app/Console/Commands holds only GenerateG2gAccessLinks, SeedG2gDefaultViewRights and SyncDataCron, and routes/console.php registers nothing). Every cross-module feed listed above would therefore have to be an inline write inside the relevant controller method - and none of those writes exist.

performance-data.ts (186 lines of mockPerformanceKPIs, mockEmployeeReviews, mockActivityFeed) is dead code imported by nothing. It is a shipping-risk leftover: its hardcoded 'Arjun Sharma / 612 employees / FY 2024-25' fixtures are the exact figures a demo would show if anyone re-wired it.
